what: Bottom clock-wheel menu — five items sit on an ellipse (radii 22% of panel width and 29% of panel height, center at 80% of panel height) in ten slots: five front and five back (shadow), each slot with its own opacity (.4·.4·.4·1·.4·.1·.05·0·.05·.1), and the current page item stands out bold at the upper-right reference slot. When going to another page, every item hops that many slots, the angle turning by joining the angles between the slots it passes (1.18s power4.inOut), and the two clock hands at bottom center (4.5rem · 8rem, −38° · −20°) make a full turn

options.current: Current page item (data-link), default is the reference item
options.from: Previous page item — when set, it starts from that spot and cycles to current (like a menu that keeps turning on sites that reload the document)
options.anchor: Order position (from 0) where the current item sits, default 3
options.stops: Opacity per slot (comma-separated, n before · n after), default .4,.4,.4,1,.4,.1,.05,0,.05,.1
options.[data-fx-part=viewport]: Oval plate — width min(80vw,800px), height min(40vw,400px), grows around the bottom center
options.[data-fx-part=item]: Item — data-link · data-angle (front slot angle) · data-ghost (back slot angle), inside <a>. The clone that circles the back position is made by the part and given data-dial-copy
options.Event fx:dial: { to, dur, ease } turn to { zoom, dur, ease } scale up to { reset: Item } set directly to it. Once it has turned all the way round, fx:clock-dial-nav { current }
